==English==

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|prudent}}, from {{der|en|fro|prudent}}, from {{der|en|la|prūdēns}}, contracted from {{m|la|prōvidēns||foresight}} ({{cog|en|providence}}), the present participle of {{m|la|prōvideō|t=to forsee; to [[provide]] for}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|prude}}. {{doublet|en|provident}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|glēaw}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|pro͞o'''′'''dənt}}{{ref|name=AHD prudent|{{R:AHD|prudent|1420|1}}}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹuː.dənt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹu.dənt/|a=GenAm,CanE}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-prudent.ogg|a=Southern California}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹʉː.dənt/|a=AuE,NZE}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹʉ.dənt/|/ˈpɹʉd.ʌnt/|a=ScE}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːdənt|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|pru|dent}}{{ref|name=AHD prudent}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{U|sagacious}} in adapting means to ends; [[circumspect]] in action, or in determining any line of conduct.
#: {{syn|en|careful|considerate|discreet|Thesaurus:cautious}}
#: {{ant|en|Thesaurus:careless|Thesaurus:reckless}}
#: {{uxa|en|It is '''prudent''' to consult a physician before beginning any new exercise regimen.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Divorce|edition=1st|<!--VIII-->|book=II|26|''Mo{{long s}}es'',{{...|Deut.24.1.}}e{{long s}}tabli{{long s}}ht a grave and '''prudent''' Law,{{nb...|full of moral equity, full of due con{{long s}}ideration towards nature, that cannot be re{{long s}}i{{long s}}ted; a Law con{{long s}}enting with the Laws of wi{{long s}}e{{long s}}t men and civile{{long s}}t nations}}.}}
#* {{quote-book|en
|year=1864
|author=Jules Verne
|title=Around the World in 80 Days
|chapter=30
|url=http://ebooks.adelaide.edu.au/v/verne/jules/v52aw/chapter30.html
|passage=He did not hesitate what to do. It would be '''prudent''' to continue on to Omaha, for it would be dangerous to return to the train, which the Indians might still be engaged in pillaging.
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120412180700/http://ebooks.adelaide.edu.au/v/verne/jules/v52aw/chapter30.html
|archivedate=12 April 2012
}}
# Practically [[wise]], [[judicious]], [[shrewd]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:wise}}
#: {{ant|en|Thesaurus:foolish}}
#: {{uxa|en|His '''prudent''' career moves reliably brought him to the top.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|22|3|3|page=739|column=2|A '''prudent''' man fore{{long s}}eeth the euill, and hideth him{{long s}}elfe: but the {{long s}}imple pa{{long s}}{{long s}}e on, and are puni{{long s}}hed.|The '''prudent''' see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.|version=NIV}}
# {{rfquote-sense|en}} {{U|frugal}}; [[economical]]; not [[extravagant]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:frugal}}
#: {{ant|en|extravagant|Thesaurus:prodigal}}
#: {{uxa|en|Only '''prudent''' expenditure may provide quality within a restrictive budget.}}

====Antonyms====
{{checksense|en}}
* {{l|en|imprudent}}
* {{l|en|incontinent}}{{ref|According to: {{cite-book|en|chapter=Book VII: Characters Other Than Virtue and Vice: X|chapterurl=https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/aristotle/nicomachean-ethics/f-h-peters/text/book-7#chapter-7-1-10|title=Nicomachean Ethics|date=2018-10-22T18:14:01.000Z|passage=It is impossible for the same man to be at once prudent and incontinent; for we have shown that man cannot be prudent without being at the same time morally good.}}}}
